ALPHABET CENTER · LETTER Y

Letter Y — Yo-yo.

A blue yo-yo swings in for the letter Y. Y glides — yuh — and spends its days going up and down, just like the toy on the card.

Meet the letter, hear its sound, trace it together — then play. Everything on this page is free, gentle and paced for you.

THE LETTER SOUND

What does Y say?

“y — yuh, like yo-yo”

Y says yuh at the start of yo-yo — a quick glide made with a wide smile. Y is a part-time letter: at the ends of words like happy it borrows the ee sound, but here it is the young consonant y.

TRACE THE LETTER

Trace Y y together.

Follow the numbers with a finger — on screen or on each other’s palms. The arrows show the way to go, the numbers show where to start, and a grown-up reads the little script below each card. Slow and wobbly is exactly right.

Trace the uppercase Y

Start at 1 at the top left, slide down to the middle. Lift. Start at 2 at the top right, slide down through the middle and straight on down.

Trace the lowercase y

Start at 1 at the top left, slide down to the bottom line. Lift. Start at 2 at the top right, slide down past the bottom line and curve the tail to the left.

TAKE IT OFF SCREEN

Yo-yo hands.

Two minutes is plenty. Follow your child’s lead and stop while it is still fun — that is the whole method.

  1. 01

    Make your hand a yo-yo: crouch down and rise up, saying yuh each time you stand.

  2. 02

    Tie a soft toy to a string and swing it gently — up, down, yuh, yuh.

  3. 03

    Count how many yo-yos you can do without laughing.

PLAY & PRACTICE

Games that use this letter.

The games mix every letter — play them after meeting two or three letters, or any day your child asks. No scores, no timers, no wrong answers that count.
